children: Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) reported blockbuster Q3 results, announced $10B research investment and new 512GB DDR5 RDIMM, secured $22B in client deals and multi‑year contracts, and benefits from surging DRAM/HBM pricing and tight industry capacity ahead of its Sept. 30 report.
Previous Week Recap
Micron Q3 Revenue, EPS Leap
: Micron (MU) Q3: revenue $41.46B, adjusted EPS $25.11, gross margin 84.9% vs 39% year-ago. Street expects Q4 roughly $31.30 EPS and ~$50.7–50.8B revenue for Sept. 30 report.
Bullish MU Targets On AI Demand
: RBC and TD Cowen kept bullish MU targets ($1,500–$1,600), citing strong AI demand for HBM, tight clean-room/EUV capacity, HBM4 roadmap, higher HBM pricing and DRAM price gains.
Client Deals Hit ~$100B RPO
: Micron (MU) reported about $22 billion in client deals and 16 multi‑year customer contracts with fixed/floored pricing, contributing to roughly $100 billion in remaining performance obligations.
Micron Research Labs $10B
: Micron (MU) plans a $10B, 10‑year investment to launch Micron Research Labs in Boise. Deirdre Hanford will lead research on memory, compute, AI, advanced packaging and next‑gen chip manufacturing.
512GB DDR5 RDIMM For Servers
: Micron unveiled a 512GB DDR5 RDIMM for servers (validated with AMD/Intel), 9,200 MT/s, 3D stacking/TSVs, ~16W per module, up to 12TB per dual‑socket server, volume H2 2027.
DRAM Prices Surged YoY
: Micron (MU): DRAM contract prices surged ~90%–95% YoY in Q1 and ~58%–63% in Q2 2026; pace of increases expected to slow in Q3, driving MU revenue and pricing outlook.
Q4 Outlook Before Sept 30
: Micron (MU) reports fiscal Q4 on Sept. 30. Traders will watch HBM pricing and shipment volumes for the next confirmed data point ahead of the release.
Gujarat Plant Starts Commercial Ops
: Micron (MU) started commercial ops at its Gujarat plant and made its first India-made memory module shipment to Dell. Plant has 500,000+ sq ft cleanroom; output set to climb in 2026–27.
Constructive Mediation With Taiwan Union
: Micron Technology (MU) and Taiwan Micron Memory Union held a constructive mediation on Sept 18; a second session is set for Oct 22 with Micron’s Taichung union participating.
Third-Largest NAND Vendor Amid Shortage
: Micron (MU) was the third-largest NAND flash vendor by Q2 revenue, trailing Samsung and SK Hynix, amid an industry memory supply shortfall projected to last through at least 2027.
